clue.text: Supply a reason for retreat

parts.note: to supply something is to give it
a ground is a reason or basis, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to justify why they withdrew.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield territory or back down in an argument is to withdraw, an idiom from battlefield movement.

clue.text: Primarily displayed by glutton, ravenously eating every delicacy

definitions.text: Primarily displayed by glutton, ravenously eating every delicacy

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of the following words are what is shown

explanation.surface: A glutton wolfs down every delicacy in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive appetite is exactly what a glutton shows when devouring every delicacy.

clue.text: Extremely frivolous signal

parts.note: very means extremely
light means frivolous, not serious

explanation.surface: A thoroughly flippant gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a coloured flare fired from a pistol, named after its inventor Edward Very.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare fired from a pistol is used to send a message at sea or in war.

clue.text: What you do with laryngitis — catch it

explanation.walkthrough: Laryngitis literally takes hold in your throat; the idiom means to be severely punished.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngitis is an inflammation of the throat, and the idiom means to be severely scolded or punished.

clue.text: Where to find an apple or a beet

parts.note: chard is a kind of beet grown for its leaves

explanation.surface: A gardener asks where an apple or a beet grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is taken as written, then chard, a leaf beet.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit trees such as apples grow in a planted enclosure of trees.

clue.text: Most generous is Ken, we hear, and happy

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for ken is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: to ken is to know, an old Scots verb
blest means blessed, happy

explanation.surface: A man called Ken is reportedly generous and cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a name but is the verb meaning know; said, KNOW gives NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble means magnanimous or high-minded, so the superlative is the most magnanimous.

clue.text: Gives a coconut as a prize

explanation.surface: A fairground stall hands out a coconut as its reward.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a coconut shy at a fair; in fact one definition is the tree that bears coconuts and the other is the old sense of a victor's award.
explanation.definitionFit: The coconut tree is a kind of tropical palm, and a palm branch was the ancient emblem of victory, so 'bear the palm' means win.

clue.text: Solitary gangster removes his hat

indicators.note: the gangster takes something off, so those letters are taken out of his name

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster
a cap is a hat

explanation.surface: A lone mobster takes off his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' is a link; taking CAP out of ALCAPONE leaves ALONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary means on one's own, without company.

clue.text: A hangover from the Christmas festivities

definitions.text: A hangover from the Christmas festivities

parts.words: A hangover from the Christmas festivities
parts.note: hangover suggests a headache after the party, but it means something literally hung over a doorway at Christmas

explanation.walkthrough: 'hangover' is read literally: a sprig hung overhead for kissing under.
explanation.definitionFit: This parasitic evergreen with white berries is traditionally hung up as a Christmas decoration.

clue.text: Strange, if socialist can come to a division

indicators.note: strange means the letters of the following words are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: Oddly, a socialist arrives at a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come to' is a link between the anagram and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Classification is the dividing of things into groups or classes.

clue.text: Unpredictable chap about to desert

indicators.note: the man's name goes around the other piece, so about signals a container here

parts.note: Eric is a typical man's name for a chap
to rat is to desert one's side

explanation.surface: A fickle man is on the point of walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to desert' reads as 'on the point of deserting'; instead 'about' puts ERIC around RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic follows no regular course, so it cannot be foreseen.

clue.text: Flute restored these sounds

explanation.surface: Someone repairs a flute and it makes noises again.
explanation.walkthrough: In an organ, the flute stop speaks only with wind from the bellows, which keep restoring the air supply; and as a verb the answer means roars.
explanation.definitionFit: Organ pipes such as a flute stop are fed air by a pumped device, and to bellow is also to shout loudly, so sounds means roars.

clue.text: Crocks ran away, turning tail before rough water

indicators.note: an army turning tail flees, but here the word for ran away is turned round end to front

parts.note: to have fled is to have run away

indicators.note: rough water is churned up, so the letters of water are disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone fled in a panic ahead of choppy seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning tail' reverses FLED to DELF; 'rough' turns WATER into TWARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocks are earthenware pots, and Dutch tin-glazed pottery from Delft is one such ware.

clue.text: Mean trick

explanation.definitionFit: Letters spell a word when they signify it, and a trick is a sailor's turn of duty at the helm, a stint of work.

clue.text: Started with live ammunition user

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a gun is the thing that fires ammunition

explanation.surface: Someone opened proceedings with a weapon loaded with real bullets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live ammunition' looks like one phrase; it splits as 'live' and 'ammunition user'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are past participles of verbs meaning commence.

clue.text: Seeing a person about the place for cargo

indicators.note: the person goes around the other piece, so about signals a container

parts.note: a being is a person or creature
a ship's hold is where cargo is stowed

explanation.surface: Someone looks round a ship's cargo store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' splits BE-ING around HOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: To behold is to see or observe, so the participle means seeing.

clue.text: Terminated in chaos — not a disadvantage

indicators.note: things in chaos are thrown into disorder, so the letters of terminated are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written: not a means this letter is left out of the jumble

explanation.surface: Something ended amid confusion, which was no bad thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes one A from the letters of TERMINATED before 'in chaos' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A detriment is harm or loss, the opposite of a benefit.

clue.text: One inured to reforms in learning

indicators.note: reforms means forms again, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A hardened person is accustomed to reform in education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is I, the Roman numeral; 'in' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is scholarly knowledge gained by study.

clue.text: Turn in to belt with heathy rough

parts.note: to belt someone is to hit them

indicators.note: rough means rearranged, so the letters of heathy are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone strikes out across rough moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining HIT to THEHAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for going to bed.

clue.text: Animal, one that dislikes swallowing paper

indicators.note: the word for a detester takes in the other piece, so swallowing signals a container

parts.note: a hater is someone who dislikes
MS, manuscript, is a paper written by hand

explanation.surface: A creature that hates eating paper.
explanation.walkthrough: MS goes inside HATER after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The hamster is a small rodent kept as a pet.

clue.text: In court a jolly bit of rigging

parts.note: a yard is a courtyard
jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: In a law court, a cheerful piece of a ship's gear is produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; 'jolly' is a noun, a Royal Marine, not cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is either end of a yard, the spar that holds a square sail.

clue.text: Season that's about to go in the wrong direction

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes around the other piece, so about signals a container

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: the verb for go is written backwards, the wrong way round

parts.note: to run is to go

explanation.surface: A season is described as about to start running backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to go' reads as 'soon to leave'; instead 'about' puts IE around NUR, RUN turned round by 'in the wrong direction'.
explanation.definitionFit: Season here is a verb: to accustom or harden someone to hardship.

clue.text: The French can afford another language

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A French speaker can manage a second tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can afford' looks like a verb phrase; 'can' is TIN and 'afford' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is a classical tongue, a different language from French.

clue.text: Bulb can be lit up

indicators.note: can be signals that the letters of lit up could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A light bulb can be switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a light bulb, matching 'lit up'; it is a flower bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips grow from bulbs, so the plant is named by its storage organ.

clue.text: Fat fighting man without a scrap retired

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the soldier goes around the other piece

parts.note: a marine is a sea soldier

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for a scrap is read backwards

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A soldier has quit the army, having never been in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: MARINE goes around GAR, RAG turned back by 'retired'.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute, an edible spread made from fats and oils.

clue.text: Bird dog lost its head

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a dog is dropped, its head cut off

parts.note: a beagle is a hunting dog

explanation.surface: A hound goes berserk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost its head' reads as panicked; it drops the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Laid up here in Calais, half of it is unlicensed

parts.note: someone laid up in bed is ill
ici is French for here, and Calais is a French port

indicators.note: the second of the two letters of it is taken, half the word

explanation.surface: Something smuggled through Calais is partly illegal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means not allowed by law or licence.

clue.text: A rebellion getting under way

parts.note: a rising is an uprising or revolt

explanation.surface: A revolt is just starting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arising is emerging or beginning to happen.

clue.text: Some yawning aperture

indicators.note: some of the letters of the phrase are taken, the run bridging the two words

explanation.surface: Part of a wide-open hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'yawning' and the start of 'aperture'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gape is a wide opening, as in a yawning mouth or chasm.

clue.text: Small change about minor characters' projection

indicators.note: the coins go around the other piece, so about signals a container

parts.note: pence are small change in British coinage

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of minor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A handful of coins mentioned beside the projecting features of minor characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' turns MINOR into ROMIN, which 'about' places inside PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominence is something that sticks out, a projection.
